headline: TauIndianBankBench reports that outcome-only scoring misses procedural failures in banking agents
summary: A paper introduces a 1,000-task synthetic Indian retail-banking benchmark for tool-using conversational agents. It scores both final database state and whether required calls—including read-only policy checks—occurred, while rejecting unrequested writes. In author-run evaluations of six models, final-state-only scoring raised pass rates by 6.5–12.0 percentage points over the paired action-plus-state criterion. The results are reported by the authors and have not been independently reproduced; simulator error, real customer behavior, non-English performance and deployment reliability remain unestablished.
